title: Shadows House
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a gothic mansion, faceless soot-covered nobles called Shadows are each served by a 'Living Doll' who acts as their face (to verify). The doll Emilico and her mistress Kate grow close as they pass the house's tests and uncover that the dolls are kidnapped human children and the Shadows' society feeds on them (to verify).
life_message: It holds up friendship, courage and seeking the truth even when an institution demands silence.

content.note: Body horror and punishments in the house (to verify; Body Horror signal).
Horror tone, conspiracy and soot monsters (to verify; AniList Conspiracy).
Drugged coffee keeps the dolls docile (to verify; Drugs signal).
Memory loss and identity erasure of children (to verify).

delivery.evidence: ANN review: foreshadowing everywhere but slow; volume one builds atmosphere and rules, hinting at class and servitude.

personified.ideology: The Shadow is master of the person

delivery.note: An ANN review describes themes of class and servitude emerging through foreshadowing rather than being stated.

winners_losers: Kate, Emilico and the dolls who resist win sympathy; the Shadow elite who exploit children lose. A worldview that questions institutional power gets sympathy.
to_verify: Violence, fear and substances recheck (2026-11-22): AniList Body Horror, Tragedy and Drugs tags not confirmed as above 3; the Age Rating Juju guide to the anime (TV-14, PG in Australia) mentions no violence, calls mind-control scenes 'intense and sad', and describes a coffee that brainwashes the dolls into loyalty rather than drug use, so all three scores stay at 3
